description: Project Sidewalk is an open-source web tool in which remote contributors walk virtually through street-level imagery and label sidewalk accessibility features and problems such as curb ramps, missing curb ramps, obstacles, surface problems and missing sidewalks; labels are validated by other users and combined into AccessScores for streets, intersections and regions. The project README reports deployments in more than 50 cities across 10 countries, including the US, Canada, Chile, India, Mexico, Ecuador, the Netherlands, Switzerland and New Zealand, and over 3.4 million labels. Coverage: the deployment cities only. Access: free API with metadata, label, validation, AccessScore and statistics endpoints returning GeoJSON or CSV; the v3 API is in preview. Licence: data dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0; source code MIT. Caveats: labels are placed on Google or Mapillary imagery whose own terms still apply, coverage and label density vary by city and imagery date, and data from removed accounts are excluded. Simulation uses: accessible pedestrian routing, sidewalk repair prioritisation and equity analysis of walkability. Related records: the DC and Arlington sidewalk condition layers and the Tile2Net sidewalk mapping tool.
